ignition.note: burning VIIRS 0.05 deg cells of that day (EquiFire archive); ignition placed at each cell CENTRE - the fire can be anywhere within the ~5 km cell

fuel.model: FM10 timber (litter and understory) + crown fire check
fuel.why: Mapped Anderson fuel models used per cell; the listed class is the fallback for unmapped cells. Land-cover to fuel and moisture conversions remain assumptions.

grid.geometry: square n x n raster centred on the ignition centroid (lon, lat); cell (row i, col j) centre = centre + ((j - n//2) * cell_m east, (i - n//2) * cell_m north), local equirectangular metres (1 deg lat = 111.32 km, lon scaled by cos(lat))

ros_note: all rates of spread multiplied by m = 3.23 (calibration on recent observed growth)

calibration.note: single spread-rate multiplier fitted to this fire's own growth over the previous days (observed = new satellite pixels, an active-fire proxy, not mapped burned area); shrunk toward 1 when the evidence is small; shared by all fires in the domain

weather.note: gridded hourly weather, 5x5 points over +-40 km

gridded.note: per-cell weather: rate of spread and wind vector computed at each weather point, bilinear to the raster cells

weather.note_time: Each simulation hour uses that hour's wind, temperature, humidity and rain; fuel moisture carries over between hours. Historical reanalysis replay is not an issued-weather-forecast backtest.

landcover.source: ESA WorldCover 2021 v200 10 m (AWS open data, keyless)

terrain.source: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (AWS open data, keyless)

landscape.barrier_note: Heuristic spread slowdown, not a calibrated probability of stopping fire.
landscape.dryness_note: Sentinel-2 moisture-index proxy mapped to assumed live-fuel moisture bins.

method.rate_of_spread: Rothermel (1972) surface spread with Albini (1976) corrections; Anderson (1982) fuel models; R = I_R*xi*(1+phi_w+phi_s)/(rho_b*eps*Q_ig)
method.crown_fire: forest only: Van Wagner (1977) initiation (CBH 4 m, FMC 100 %) and active-crown criterion (CBD 0.15 kg/m3); crown ROS = 3.34 x FM10 ROS with WAF 0.4 (Rothermel 1991)
method.wind: hour-specific 10 m wind / 1.15 -> 20 ft wind (Lawson & Armitage 2008) x wind adjustment factor (Albini & Baughman 1979 unsheltered; 0.15 under forest canopy, Andrews 2012)
method.slope: phi_s = 5.275*beta^-0.3*tan^2(slope) (Rothermel 1972), vector-summed with wind (Finney 1998); terrain from Open-Meteo elevation API (Copernicus DEM 90 m) sampled on a 15x15 grid
method.fuel_moisture: Simard (1968) EMC from T and RH; 1/10/100 h time-lag fuels; rain wetting heuristic M += (35-M)(1-exp(-P/P_i)), P_i = 0.5/2/10 mm; live herb 60 %, live woody 100 % (assumed)
method.shape: ellipse, length-to-breadth from effective mid-flame wind (Anderson 1983), fire at rear focus
method.growth: time-dependent minimum-travel-time raster (cf. Finney 2002), exact Dijkstra, 16 neighbours
method.envelope: low = wind x0.8 & RH +10; high = wind x1.2 & RH -10 (same grid for small fires, else 2x coarser grid with ignition area rescaled; clipped so low <= central <= high); a sensitivity range, not a calibrated probability
method.fires: ignition cells split into fires A, B, C ... (1 km gap rule); per-fire area = cells reached first by that fire's front; merge = first contact of two fires' burned areas
method.calibration: one rate-of-spread multiplier m fitted to the fire's own observed growth over the previous 1-3 days (physics re-run over that window with its weather; VIIRS pixels, + GOES 2 km pixels if goes=on in the Americas), Bayesian shrinkage toward 1 (prior sd ln 3), clipped 0.1..5; applied to the forward run
method.weather_grid: weather=grid: 5x5 Open-Meteo points over +-40 km; moisture, ROS and wind vector per point, bilinear to cells (equifire.fireweather)
method.fwi: Canadian FWI System for the start date (equifire.fireweather.fwi_for, cffdrs equations), context only
method.landscape: landscape=on: mapped WorldCover Anderson fuel groups, Copernicus terrain, heuristic OSM firebreak slowdown and Sentinel-2 live-moisture bins where available; fallback explicitly reported
method.noaa_fallback: public NOAA GFS 0.25 degree regional GRIB, 3-hourly source interpolated hourly; vector wind interpolation; PRATE approximates hourly rainfall; older cycles for moisture spin-up

uncertainty: Experimental screening estimate. Fuel mapping and live-moisture conversions are assumptions; landscape coverage can be partial. Firebreaks use heuristic slowdown, not calibrated stop probabilities. No suppression, spotting or explicit solar fuel heating. Weather is much coarser than the simulation raster. Low/high are sensitivity scenarios, not probability bounds. Prior validation reports apply to the older physics pipeline; the landscape update has not established improved predictive accuracy.

fwi.source: Open-Meteo (archive ERA5 + forecast best-match), noon LST approx = solar noon
fwi.note: Canadian Forest Fire Weather Index System (Van Wagner 1987, cffdrs equations), daily at local noon, 60-day spin-up; reported for context and as a moisture cross-check, NOT used by the spread model
